A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Interlat. All 21 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison through readable text and rendered figures, tables, and equations.

before.justification: V1 reports original ALFWorld experiments, including benchmark comparisons, latent perturbations, compression results, training analyses, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original ALFWorld results and adds LLaMA and cross-family evaluations, MATH results, and PCA analyses of latent communication.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, and compression procedure are retained. Section 3.2 reverses the displayed curriculum mixture from latent-prefix/text-suffix to text-prefix/latent-suffix, but v1's prose already describes replacement from the left. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects the equation or changes the implemented training procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates ALFWorld only. V2 retains it and adds MATH, with overall and difficulty-specific results in Table 2, extending coverage from interactive household planning to non-interactive mathematical reasoning.

E2.justification: The corresponding ALFWorld comparisons retain CoT (full), No-CoT, Text, No-Comm, and the same perturbation controls. MATH uses the existing task comparators. The added Qwen2LLaMA row evaluates a model-pair configuration of Interlat.

E3.justification: V2 adds LLaMA3.1-8B and Qwen-to-LLaMA configurations, difficulty-stratified MATH evaluation, and a 3,119-sample PCA/adapter comparison. It also changes the reported Qwen7B separation-loss weight range from [0.1, 2.0] to [0.1, 1.0], without establishing that experiments were rerun. The ALFWorld splits and 20-step limit remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds PCA clustering and centroid-shift analyses testing task structure and adapter effects (Appendix I), and extends perturbation and compression analyses to LLaMA. The original component ablations and extended 32-step parallelism analysis are retained after relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over three independent runs and use uncertainty values in compression and ablation tables. V2 extends these practices to additional results without reporting increased run counts, new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New ALFWorld results report 70.71%/70.90% seen/unseen success for LLaMA and 70.95%/71.39% for Qwen2LLaMA (Table 1). New MATH results show Interlat below CoT overall, 36.88% versus 38.35%, but above it on Level 5, 15.80% versus 15.05% (Table 2). LLaMA compression and PCA statistics are added; matching Qwen table values are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the mathematical definition of the curriculum mixture by reversing which positions contain token embeddings and latent states. The compression losses already appear in v1 Appendix A and remain in v2 Appendix B; their expanded main-text presentation introduces no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The feasibility, exploration, and compression claims remain. V2 adds explicit claims of cross-family compatibility and operation without parameter sharing or architectural coupling. Cross-family integration moves from future work in v1's conclusion to a reported capability; the 24-fold speedup claim already existed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for MATH's difficulty-dependent results using linguistic regularization versus premature reasoning collapse, interprets cross-family results as transferable latent understanding, and interprets PCA shifts as task-aware semantic alignment. These mechanisms and the acknowledged MATH disadvantage extend the largely retained exploration and compression interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 adds training/inference pseudocode, explicit truncation and model-role descriptions, and PCA processing details. Much of Appendix C relocates existing settings. V1's actor training times of 6 and 3.3 hours, reasoner training time of 8–48 hours, and explicit LayerNorm-plus-Linear bridge specification are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against emergent communication, autoencoder-based thought exchange, and parameter-, memory-, or cache-sharing approaches, citing Lazaridou/Tucker, Zheng, Christianos, Salemi, and Fu/Zou. It adds an agent-autonomy distinction while removing the human mind-reading literature and Su et al. curriculum citation.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 replaces much of the mind-reading terminology, adds contribution bullets, promotes compression to a separate section, moves detailed settings into appendices, and introduces an appendix contents page.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text, expands Table 1, and adds MATH, LLaMA, and PCA displays plus algorithm blocks. Existing figures are resized or relocated. Figure 3 drops its cross-entropy panel, and Figure 6 shows three panels although its caption still describes six steps.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens v1's Qwen-only ALFWorld evidence with cross-family tests and MATH results that reveal both benefits and an overall CoT advantage. Expanded objective explanations and pseudocode improve clarity. The net gain is limited by unspecified MATH backbone and evaluation details, untested explanations for its difficulty-dependent results, and removal of training-time information.
